comment: He's a great professor and a very good lecturer. However, the course is set up so that points are based on tests and quizzes, with assigned homework that doesn't count for points. If you have a very solid prior understanding of calculus, then you should take this course. Also, the best way to succeed is to ABUSE his office hours.

For anyone considering him, make sure to also read the ratings for JAMES David, as it is the same prof and has more extensive ratings. Take it from someone who made the mistake of not reading those....

He goes through material so fast. If you haven't taken BC/aren't a math major...good luck. I got an A+ in Cal1 here so I was really caught off guard. Maybe he's a good prof to math majors but he doesn't really explain anything and does more "teach by example." Also weekly timed quizzes which are a grade tanker without any classwork/homework grades.

Dr. Davis is very passionate about math, but sometimes he gets on tangents that aren't entirely related to our course material. Class moves fast, and the weekly quizzes + the three tests can be very difficult. His office hours are at 8am, which is rough, but he is very helpful, understanding, and caring if you actually go in and ask questions.

Dr. Davis is incredibly sweet and a great teacher. This class is pretty difficult, but you'll learn a ton. He goes over a lot of info quickly, so homework always takes a while, but there's time to ask questions at the beginning of class and he's v accessible outside of class. If you like math and you are willing to work for an A, you'll like it.

A really great professor. He can be a little dry and hard to read at times but he really knows his stuff and is clearly passionate about the subject. Very helpful outside of class and gives extra credit for attending university talks. This is a very hard course so just make sure you dont get behind and he'll help make sure you don't.

He refuses to work with you for academic accommodations and is not receptive to feedback from disability services. Please stay away from him if you have any kind of accommodation because it becomes extremely stressful and hard to learn under these conditions.

Good professor who knows math well. Regular tests and quizzes, and extra credit for attending department lectures. Clear explanations but you have to be switched on and listening at all times or else you'll be lost. Recommend for those who like math and calculus already as I can imagine it being significantly harder and less engaging otherwise.

don't take him if there are other options. he's fine in office hours (that are 8-9am) but his lectures are unclear and many homework problems don't have solutions. he will also assign homework problems and later say we never need to know that information. quizzes every week and tests are fair, but lectures hard to follow.

Class with Dr Jim Davis was possibly the most difficult, but most rewarding i've ever had. I truly was challenged to learn the material— and even with a C- this is the most math I've ever learnt.

He is a caring professor and will help you, if you ask. Make sure to study and get ahead. You will learn a LOT. Tough grader but he wishes for fluency.

Be ready to put in the time and brainpower. Linear Algebra with Jim Davis is definitely a challenge; if you're up for it, you'll be just fine. He's hilarious, brilliant, and honestly? I'd grab a beer with him. You WILL learn linear algebra in this class. If you're looking for something that pushes you but really teaches you, this is it.

Linear Algebra with Dr. Davis was brutal. Probably the worst class I've ever taken at UR. No homework, but weekly quizzes and 3 exams + a cumulative final — all without a formula sheet. No extra credit. His lectures are dry, and he doesn't explain complex topics well. Be ready to self-teach or, better yet, avoid this class entirely if you can.

Linear algebra with Jim Davis will make you work your ass off, but it's rewarding if you stick with it. You'll come out much stronger in math. Be prepared to put in the time, and you'll be fine. I also found him quite funny and a nice guy.

Lectures are always hard to follow and exams are super hard. He is definitely smart, but that does not mean that he has good teaching skills. It is absolutely impossible to get an A unless you've learnt Calculous before or you are a genius. The class average is around 78%, so if you want to kill your GPA and drain yourself, then choose his classes.

I got a 5 on AP Calc BC and this class was a doozy. The ungraded homework had answers to every other problem, and the homework and class notation was often very different. This was a problem because he didn't lecture much, since homework questions and weekly quizzes would take up half of weekly class time. 8-10 am office hours. Interesting content.

Dr. Davis made calculus II a lot harder than it needed to be. He assigns homework that does not always correlate with the lectures. When he takes questions over it the next class, there are lots, so it cuts into lecture time, creating new problems. There were lots of ups and downs with different units, with mostly downs. Overall, not worth it.

Dr Davis is a brilliant mathematician. He was always prepared for class and receptive to questions. Because he had such a good understanding of the concepts he was teaching, in my opinion, he could go be difficult to follow at times. He was always helpful during office hours. Do the homework and watch videos about the material between classes.
Horrible experience
Never ever again.

Dr. Davis is a great teacher in my experience and it's not hard to do well on his quizzes and tests if you actually study and pay attention. People who say otherwise on here probably aren't willing to put in enough effort.

Do not take Dr. Davis. He made a class that should not have been that hard almost impossible to do well in. The tutors provided by the school did not know how to do his test/quiz questions. Do not take him.
Professor Davis is excellent at explaining the material and making students care, even if it is a challenging course. I personally found him rather funny as well

Horrible experience honestly. Office hours at 8 am on Monday, quizes every weeks, unpredictable tests. He covers million different topics, so be ready to take not one class, but four classes. Lots of material on physics, biology, statistics and more. Try to avoid this professor

Professor Davis is not necessarily a "tough grader". Actually, his quiz questions are based on hw and notes, and test questions are based on quizzes. Not hard to get a good grade if you really spend time studying every single hw question and note. However, it takes A LOT of time outside of class.

The most awful professor I have ever seen. One week one quiz, but no clear class is given because of his poor teaching ability. Chatted with several guys and most of them felt difficult and confused about the content. Heavily based on quizzes and exams makes the situation worse. I hardly not fail it and will recommend everyone to avoid him

Some reviews mention Prof Davis' outdated teaching style, but I found it straightforward. 10 quizzes, 3 tests, and a final, plus knowing homework questions beforehand, it's manageable with effort. He's not only smart and helpful but also great outside class. Just grind out every homework questions and get your "A". It's truly a grind/hustle class.

Dr. Davis has one of the most outdated teaching style and class structures makes the class extremely difficult and not rewarding at all. His structure makes it so that the exams count for everything since homework and attendance isn't graded. Even his calc 2 sections are unnecessarily difficult

Professor Davis has an outdated style of teaching that students just do not understand. The class is rigorous and extremely difficult, and he expects you to know everything after showing just a single example. He moves very fast and won't stop just because you are struggling. His tests/quizzes are near impossible, DO NOT take this class.

Dr. Davis is a rlly nice guy and cares about his students. Doesn't have fluff points but gives 10 quizzes and drops lowest 5. Not the best at lecturing in class but if you go to office hours he explains everything super well. However, if math doesn't rlly click for you then take a diff teacher bc you'll have to put in lots of extra work

Professor Jim Davis is the worst professor I have ever had. His class is extremely difficult & almost impossible to pass unless you are a genius. He is a horrible lecturer & teacher. Even with meeting w/ him every week, doing the optional hw, & studying I constantly failed. This class will kill your GPA & drain you. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!

Prof. Davis is a brilliant man, you can truly see he is passionate about Mathematics. He is also available for questions, so that's also a big plus. The class has 3 exams and 10 weekly quizzes (he drops the 5 lowest grades) so you need to keep up and do your homework (it's optional but VERY useful).

Dr. Davis is a good teacher who cares about what he is teaching, but the class can be quite stressful. His office hours are at inconvenient times, especially if you have questions about one of the weekly quizzes he gives. He doesn't offer re-takes but he only keeps 5 quizzes. HW doesn't count so it matters how well you do on the assessments

jim davis is an absolutely great guy. highly suggest this class for calc, we have 10 quizzes all semester and he drops your 5 lowest quizzes... take this guy. homework is not graded, but i suggest doing it. while he may not be the best at teaching the material he is a great guy and the quiz drops surely help, he also offers extra credit. take jim.

Dr. Davis is a brilliant mathematician, but a terrible professor, unless you're a genius. I'm an average good math major who really enjoys the subject despite its challenges. I had a very hard time understanding his lectures and my mental health was not in a good state bc of this class. There are much better profs in the Math Dept that you can take

the nicest professor! His grading is clear and is pretty much based on weekly quizzes and 4 main tests. The quizzes are often problems that were found in the hw(which technically is optional but u really should do if u want a good grade) The course content is hard, but if you spend time doing the hw you will be good! Literally the nicest man ever

Dr. Davis does all his class notes by hand on a chalkboard so the only way to learn the material is to show up for class. If you pay close attention during his lectures he gives lots of hints about quiz/test questions. Always available in his office. Super friendly and helpful. By week 2 you'll be able to predict what questions he'll ask on exams.

Dr. Davis is clearly very intelligent and a very kind man, but he is probably the worst teacher I have ever had. He gives us tough quizzes directly after teaching us new material, so nobody has had the chance to learn it well and most people do very poorly. If you don't want to kill your GPA and overdose on stress I would not recommend this class.
Calculus 2 is a very tedious class and Dr. Davis made it even worse!! Brilliant guy, though I'm not sure if I would take his class again.

Pay attention and make sure you do all the homework and understand the why of how things work in Calculus. Just getting the right answer isn't acceptable with Dr. Davis. However, he is one of the nicest professors I've met and is very easy to meet with.

Really good professor. Clearly tells us what he expects for his weekly quizzes (which are very good for actually learning the course material) and takes 5 best ones out of 10. He assigns textbook problems and later discusses them and gives easier ways to do them sometimes. Tests are hard, but not impossible if you do the homework assigned.

Easily the best Math professor at UofR. He's really nice and tries his best to break down the hardest of topics. Tests are tough, mostly because material is difficult, not that he is. Do the homework assigned (he tends to reuse questions on quizzes and tests). Gives 10 quizzes and only uses top 5. Great guy.

Davis is the best math teacher I've ever had but also the hardest. Always welcomes me for office hours and really wants you to do well. Having said that, this class is extremely hard and if you don't put in the work you will fail. He expects a lot and you will most likely bomb your first exam but if you keep at it you should see grades improve.

Dr. Davis gives tough quizzes, but makes up for it by dropping two. Tests aren't easy or hard: as someone who did pretty well in high school calc, I averaged about a 90 on them. Class is definitely manageable and he teaches the material well and makes himself amply available if you're struggling to keep up. Missed 10+ classes and it didn't matter.
He is very nice, very clear, and cares a lot about his students, but he ripped my sanity apart piece by piece. Do not take this class with Dr. Davis
Clear lectures, fair grading. He is helpful during office hours. Do the homework consistently because he puts homework problems on the quizzes and tests, sometimes word for word.
Dr. Davis is simply amazing. If you dont like him its just becuase you cant do math and you will hate it with any professor. He is so helpful and very dedicated.

Easily the best professor in the department. He is extremely clear and is very willing to help outside of class. His tests are hard, but fair and very consistent with the lectures and homework. If you put in the effort, you can learn a tremendous amount. Also a phenomenal person: very kind with a great sense of humor.

I have just finished Linear Algebra's second mind-term. It was so hard and a disater. Nobody can finish all the questions in time. I promise he never do his test by himself.  He assigned a great amount of hw. But in class, you can only learn very few knowledge. I study this course totally  by self-study.

Explains everything you need to know to get A on the test, but grades harshly.(majority gets C) does not try to trick you. Final is much easyer then tests. Homework is hard, and he dos not test you on it. Overall, one of best profs. at richmond. If you make a low 90 for class, you will get bumped up to an A.

Davis is a good teacher.  The material he teaches is not always easy, but he teaches it well.  He works out a lot of examples and proofs in class, and is more than willing to go over them with you outside of class.  Tests can be pretty difficult, but I've always felt well-prepared.  All in all, he's a good guy and a decent teacher.

Dr. Davis is a brilliant professor and a great guy. I've found that Davis is a great teacher who can give you a really concrete understanding of the material if you are willing to do the work he assigns--which isn't ever too lengthy, but crucial. He's typically very lenient about due dates and extremely approachable.  One of the best I've ever had.

Good guy, but does not know how to teach for his life. He expects everyone to know exactly what he's doing in class. He puts probably one example up and assigns problems for hw he never taught in class. Hw is graded for correctness so everyone pretty much fails and his tests are ridiculous.

calc 1-really nice guy, but rushes in class, expects you to have a strong knowledge of calc before coming to the class, but very helpful outside of class.  he lets you drop your 2 lowest quiz and hw grades, which helps alot. quizzes pretty straightforward, but tests are impossible-you need to be naturally good at calculus to do well

Calculus II ...... knows what he's talking about, but classes are hard to follow at times.  Collects homework weekly for completion and correctness.  Quizzes and tests are straightforward, but studying is a must.
I would say that he thinks people know more than they do... Very approachable and very nice guy.... If you know a little going into his class it will help a LOT.  NOt bad overall and def a goood guy

Very difficult. Frequently makes small errors in arithematic that confuse the subject matter. Uses an assistant to check homework for accuracy, not for completion or effort. Often assigns homework on material not covered in class until the next day. Tough grader, and harsh with partial credit.

worst professor ever. I had him for May term. He regularly taught us the WRONG way to do a problem only to correct himself just minutes before a test or quiz. He used dirogatory comments in lessons like"you can't trust someone who makes minimum wage" & "if you're poor you can't get a loan at a bank" He is a terrible teacher & tough grader. BOOOOOO!

Davis is a nice guy and he's pretty helpful. His tests are really hard compared to his quizzes and the homework.. hm. Generally, a good class. He teaches on a higher level than most of his students are at, so you have to ask him questions constantly.

He is very helpful out of class if you go and talk to him, but he assumes students know more than they do.  The class was very challenging, but he helped me get through it.  I would definitely take it again, he is willing to help and explain things.  He also pushes back HW and discusses it in class.
Great teacher! Demanding and extremely professional, always very helpful. He's hard but you definitely learn and appreciate his toughness later!
He assigns homework and then teaches what you've learned the next day.  Taking a class with him is like trying to teach yourself calculus out of your book.  That's not what I'm here for.

Davis was a really nice guy who was ready and willing to help with problems at any times.  His tests and quizzes were hard, and his hand-in homeworks were always a guaranteed lowering of your grade, but overall he was a good teacher and the class was above average.
No Comments
No Comments
He's a good teacher and I see him at church sometimes. The class is hard, I def. fell behind, but it is possible to get a good grade if you listen to his cues. He's just flat out a good guy
Dr. Davis is the most outstanding teacher I have had and a great role model.
No Comments
